newsitem.title: GERMANY: German '97 building investment to fall one pct - Ifo.
newsitem.headline: German '97 building investment to fall one pct - Ifo.

text.p: Germany's Ifo research institute said in a study released on Friday that total construction investment in Germany fell 2.5 percent in 1996 and that it expected a further fall of one percent this year.
It put total German construction spending at 410.0 billion marks in 1996, dropping to 406.9 billion this year and 405.9 billion the year after.
It added, however, that an improvement in the economy and jobs market should from 1998 lead to an end in declining investment, at least in the west of the country.

"Private consumption will as a result of improved employment increase more quickly than in this year and the decline in building investment should be halted," Willi Leibfritz, head of Ifo's macroeconomic and public finance division said in a statement.
"Above all, commercial building in the west should be increasingly buoyant (from 1998)," he continued in the text of a speech to be delivered at a construction industry conference in Leipzig.
West German building investment was expected to remain at 1996 levels over the course of this year, with a continued decline in east German spending leading to the overall shortfall, Ifo forecast.
East German investment, which initially rose strongly after unification in 1990, would continue to fall by around two percent in 1997 and three percent next year, it added.
"This trend downwards will continue until the end of the millenium," the research institute forecast in its study.
